content:
The image shows a mango leaf with distinct small, dark raised spots/pustules scattered across the leaf surface. These are black, roughly circular lesions, some appearing slightly raised or sunken. The leaf margin is intact but shows some browning near the tips. No white powdery coating, no sooty black coating, no galls, no stem dieback visible.

Key features:
- Small, dark (black/brown) discrete spots on leaf surface
- Some spots appear slightly raised or water-soaked
- Scattered distribution across the leaf
- Affects the leaf lamina

This pattern is most consistent with **Anthracnose** — which on mango causes small, dark, angular to circular spots on leaves. Bacterial Canker can also cause dark spots but tends to have a more water-soaked halo. Sooty Mould would show a continuous black coating. Powdery Mildew shows white powdery growth. Cutting Weevil and Gall Midge cause physical damage/distortion. Die Back affects stems/branches.

The discrete, dark, scattered spots on the leaf blade match Anthracnose most closely.
